designs.title: Probably Fine
designs.why: I drive an old car, so I laughed right away. A wall of lit warning lights with a calm PROBABLY FINE is a joke anyone who has owned a beater gets in one second. The big headline carries it from across a room, and it looks clean and graphic on the black tee, not cheesy. The tiny labels are only readable up close, but they're a nice reward when someone leans in.
designs.fix: Make the icon grid a bit bigger relative to the headline (or the labels a touch bolder) so the lights read clearly at arm's length rather than shrinking to a gray texture on the tee.

designs.title: How to Go to Bed
designs.why: Exactly what my dog does every night. Four 'Turn around' steps and the final '7. Sigh.' made me smile, and the loose brush drawings are warm and cute without being childish. It's gentle and wearable on both tees. From a distance it reads as small dog doodles, though, so the joke only lands when someone gets close enough to read the steps.
designs.fix: Scale the whole print up and make the step captions larger and heavier so the repeated 'Turn around.' can be read from a few steps away. That repetition is the punchline.

designs.title: The Box
designs.why: Every cat owner has lived this: you buy the nice bed and the cat picks the box. The drawings are lovely, clear and well paced, and the smug cat in panel 3 is great. But the caption is tiny and its wording made me stop and think. 'Box not sold separately' is a bit backwards, so the tagline adds confusion instead of a final laugh. The pictures already tell the story better than the words do.
designs.fix: Make the caption bigger and say it plainly, e.g. 'BED SOLD SEPARATELY. BOX INCLUDED.' or 'THE BOX WAS FREE', so the last line lands as the punchline instead of a puzzle.
